title: Best Car Shampoo UK
short: Seven car shampoos tested for foam, cleaning power and lubrication, including dragging a microfibre cloth across a rinsed bonnet to check for swirl risk, from 6p to 70p a wash.
intro: The wrong car shampoo can leave fine swirl marks in your paintwork even if it looks clean afterwards, which is why lubrication matters as much as suds. This guide is based on Auto Express's tested roundup (8 January 2026), where testers assessed foam quality, cleaning power against sprayed-on oil, and crucially lubrication, measured by dragging a microfibre cloth across a rinsed bonnet to judge how slippery, and therefore how safe for the paint, each shampoo felt. Cost-per-wash was calculated from each product's dilution rate and bottle size for a standard 10-litre bucket.

products.name: Auto-Wash
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best cleaning and lubrication regardless of upfront cost
products.key_spec: 500ml bottle, effective from just 5ml per bucket, 17-34p per wash
products.summary: Auto Express's overall winner, rated a full 5 stars for exceptional results even at a minimal 5ml dose per bucket. Using the recommended double dose gave excellent foam and the best lubrication on test, with outstanding cleaning power against the oil-spray test, meaning its high concentration makes it genuinely cost-effective despite the higher-looking upfront price.
pros: Best lubrication on test, lowest swirl risk
Highly concentrated, so cheap per wash despite the price
cons: Highest bottle price on test upfront

products.name: pH Neutral Shampoo
products.best_for: Buyers who want top-tier performance with a convenient pop-up cap
products.key_spec: 500ml bottle, 1:1000 dilution, pop-up cap, 18p per wash
products.summary: Auto Express rated this 4.5 stars, needing only tiny amounts thanks to an extreme 1:1000 dilution rate. A pop-up cap helps prevent spillage during dosing, and testers found strong initial foam that returns when reapplied, plus good grease-cutting performance and satisfactory lubrication just behind the class-leading Bilt-Hamber.
pros: Strong foam that returns on reapplication
cons: Lubrication slightly behind the class-leading Bilt-Hamber

products.name: Shampoo & Wax
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong value at a low price and don't mind using more per wash
products.key_spec: 2 litre bottle, 30ml per bucket, widely available at Tesco, 13p per wash
products.summary: Auto Express rated this 4 stars and called it excellent value despite needing a higher 30ml dose per bucket than the concentrated leaders. Testers were surprised by strong lubrication for the price, with reasonable foam, and it's widely available in supermarkets like Tesco.
pros: Surprisingly strong lubrication for the price
cons: Needs a higher dose per wash than concentrated rivals

products.name: Bodywork Shampoo
products.best_for: Buyers who hand-dry their car and want fewer water marks
products.key_spec: 1 litre bottle, rinse-aid formula, 30p per wash
products.summary: Auto Express rated this 3.5 stars as a solid mid-table performer, with a rinse-aid formula that noticeably reduces water spotting as the car dries, useful if you don't dry it by hand straight away. Lubrication scored a little below the top three, so care is still needed to avoid swirl marks.
cons: Lubrication slightly below the top three
Pricier per wash than the leaders

guide.q: Why does lubrication matter more than foam?
guide.a: Auto Express measured this directly by dragging a microfibre cloth across a rinsed bonnet: a shampoo that feels slippery is cushioning dirt particles away from the paint as you wash, reducing the risk of fine swirl marks. A shampoo that produces lots of foam but poor lubrication, like the Tesco option Auto Express tested, can actually increase swirl risk even though the car looks clean afterwards.

guide.q: Does a higher price mean better value?
guide.a: Not necessarily. Auto Express calculated a genuine cost-per-wash for each shampoo based on its dilution rate, and found the pricier-looking Bilt-Hamber worked out competitive with cheaper bottles because so little is needed per wash, while some low-price bottles needed much larger doses to perform.

guide.q: Do I need a specific shampoo if my car has a ceramic coating or wax?
guide.a: Auto Express's test focused on cleaning power, foam and lubrication rather than any claimed protective coatings in the shampoos themselves, so if you rely on a separate wax or ceramic coating for protection, prioritise a shampoo like the Bilt-Hamber or VP with proven high lubrication to avoid degrading that layer through swirling.

guide.q: Is a shampoo-and-wax combo worth it?
guide.a: The Simoniz Shampoo & Wax scored well in Auto Express's testing and adds a light wax layer during washing, useful for topping up protection between full details, though a dedicated wax or sealant will typically last longer and protect better than a wash-in formula.
